SK2131 The get-only property is never assigned

A property with only a get accessor, no initializer and no constructor that assigns it can be written from nowhere, so it holds default for the life of every instance.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0
ReSharperUnassignedGetOnlyAutoProperty (resharper_unassigned_get_only_auto_property_highlighting)

Why

⚠ This is the one shape of issue #24 the compiler leaves entirely alone, and the narrowing was measured rather than argued. A probe built at AnalysisMode=All reports CS0649 for a private, an internal and a private readonly field that nothing assigns, so the field half of the concept belongs to the compiler and there is nothing to add. A public field draws no CS0649 and cannot: any consumer outside the compilation may write it, so the claim is not decidable here either. What remains is the property half, and it is decidable for a reason worth stating — a property with only a `get` accessor and no initializer can be assigned from nowhere but a constructor of its own declaring type, every part of that type is in this compilation because a type cannot be split across assemblies, and a source generator's part is compiled source like any other. "Nothing assigns it" is therefore a fact this analysis establishes rather than a guess about callers, which is the difference between this rule and the field half it declines.

Example

Instead of:

sealed class Window {
    public int Width { get; }        // nothing ever assigns it: always 0

    public bool IsWide => Width > 800;
}

Write:

sealed class Window {
    public int Width { get; }

    public Window(int width) => Width = width;

    public bool IsWide => Width > 800;
}

The ReSharper mapping

The export carries six inspections for issue #24's concept — UnassignedField.Global, UnassignedField.Local, UnassignedReadonlyField, UnassignedGetOnlyAutoProperty, NotNullOrRequiredMemberIsNotInitialized and PropertyFieldKeywordIsNeverAssigned. Skala ships the fourth and only the fourth, and the reason is measured rather than a matter of taste: the three field inspections describe what CS0649 already reports, and --resharper-severities maps the one inspection this rule actually covers. The others have no Skala id and none is proposed until somebody can say what they would add to the compiler.

When it does not fire

⚠ A non-nullable reference type under nullable warnings is declined, because `CS8618` already reports it — verified on the same probe, with an explicit constructor and with an implicit one. ADR-008 makes hosting a platform diagnostic the right outcome, and a second finding on the same declaration under a Skala id would be the same defect counted twice. What survives the exclusion is everything CS8618 cannot see, and the probe measured that too: a value type, a nullable reference type, and any get-only property in a nullable-oblivious file all draw nothing at all from the compiler. ⚠ The annotation half of the nullable context is deliberately not consulted, only the warning half — a file with annotations on and warnings off gets no CS8618, and that is a real configuration in which this rule is the only thing that will speak. An unconstrained type parameter falls on the declined side, which is the conservative direction. ⚠ The declaring type is walked through its symbol rather than through the file the finding is in, so a partial part in generated source — the generator that writes the constructor — is read even though the analyzer does not report in generated code; a rule that skipped those parts would fire on every generated-constructor type, which is the wall that closed #114 and #115. The residue in front of which no compilation-local analysis can go is reflection: FieldInfo.SetValue against the compiler-generated backing field writes the property from outside the language, and no analyzer can see it. ⚠ A positional record property is never examined, by construction rather than by a filter — this rule reads a property declaration, and a positional record's property has none, because the parameter is where it is written down; no test on IsImplicitlyDeclared is performed, and the shape would be declined anyway because a positional property is { get; init; }. An expression-bodied property, a property carrying any attribute, an abstract or extern one, and anything with a set or init accessor are all outside the shape. Report-only: the property is permanently default and saying what it should be instead is the one thing the declaration does not contain. Generated code is excluded.
